pattern: definite article the + noun (a known or unique thing)
adjective before the noun, never changing form (adj + noun)
am/is/are links the subject to a noun or adjective; never left out (she is a teacher, not she teacher)
indefinite article a/an + singular countable noun (an before a vowel sound; never with uncountables like advice, information)
exampleGloss: one idea, not a specific one

pattern: present simple, he/she/it: verb + -s (-es after s/sh/ch/x/o: watches, goes; -ies: studies; have → has)
exampleGloss: this is her regular job or habit

pattern: possessive 's for people/animals: owner + 's + thing (plural owners: the boys' room; for things prefer of: the door of the house)
exampleGloss: the house that belongs to the man

pattern: prepositions of place: in (inside), on (surface), at (point; fixed: at home, at work)
exampleTarget: in the house, on the table, at home
exampleGloss: inside the house, on top of the table, at one's home

pattern: present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing for actions happening now (not with state verbs: know, like, want, have = own)
present simple questions and negatives with do/does/don't/doesn't + base verb (verb loses -s; no do with be/can: Are you…? isn't, can't)
exampleTarget: do you read books? he doesn't read
exampleGloss: a question about your reading habit; reading is not something he does

pattern: regular past simple: verb + -ed for a finished action (stopped, studied; regular verbs only, irregular keep their own form: went, had, saw)
exampleGloss: our work happened earlier and is finished

pattern: present perfect have/has + past participle for experience or a state up to now (for/since; ever): I have lived here since 2020, not I live here since 2020
exampleTarget: I have lived here for two years
exampleGloss: I moved here two years ago and still live here
